newsitem.title: CHINA: UPS leases DC-10 for trans-Pacific backup.
newsitem.headline: UPS leases DC-10 for trans-Pacific backup.

text.p: United Parcel Service has chartered a McDonnell Douglas DC-10 freighter to maintain its trans-Pacific express shipment service from Hong Kong, UPS Hong Kong manager Perry Chao told Reuters.
UPS pilots who operate an ex-Hong Kong daily trans-Pacific Boeing 747 freighter service refused to cross picket lines during the ongoing strike of UPS Teamster employees in the U.S.
Chao declined to name the airline leasing the aircraft.
He said UPS in Hong Kong had suffered a drop in business but declined to say by how much.
"A lot of our customers are staying loyal but obviously some don't want to take the risk. Customers have been concerned about proof of delivery and there has been a drop in business," Chao said.
UPS has also removed its next day delivery guarantee because of the disruption caused by the US walkout over pay.
As part of its emergency contingency plans, UPS is also using scheduled airlines to provide extra uplift and get freight to its destination and Chao said this meant increased expense.
The company was focusing on international shipments only and was trying to avoid its US network and routing traffic through Europe as much as possible to keep shipments flowing, he added.
Despite the strike, Chao added that international shipments into the US are still being delivered on time as managers man work stations.
